A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same Variational Diffusion Unlearning (VDU) work despite the changed title and publication format. Their complete main texts, equations, tables, figures, and appendices support reliable comparison.

before.justification: V2 reports original class-unlearning experiments on MNIST, CIFAR-10, and tinyImageNet, CelebA feature-unlearning results, and Stable Diffusion experiments, including quantitative and qualitative appendix results.

after.justification: V4 retains these original experiments and adds epoch-dependent results, CLIP measurements, baseline timing measurements, and experiments with limited retained-data access.

M1.justification: The variational objective, two-term loss in Equation 2, gradient-update algorithm, and checkpoint-based parameter estimation remain unchanged. Additional retained-data fine-tuning is evaluated as a supplementary experimental condition, rather than introduced into the core VDU algorithm.

E1.justification: V4 adds Thomas Kinkade artistic-style targets to the Stable Diffusion evaluation in Figure 10. The existing datasets and class/feature tasks remain, including CelebA already evaluated in v2 Appendix A.2.2. UnlearnCanvas is mentioned as future evaluation, not actually tested.

E2.justification: Table 1 retains fine-tuning, Selective Amnesia, SalUn, and ESD. The CelebA comparison retains fine-tuning, SalUn, and ESD in both versions. Added comparisons reuse existing unlearning baselines; no new comparison method or substantive baseline adaptation is introduced.

E3.justification: Existing benchmark protocols remain. Added protocols include CLIP ViT-B/32 evaluation after five style-unlearning or ten object-unlearning epochs, an epochs 1–5 study stated to use gamma 0.3, and one epoch of additional fine-tuning using 50 retained-data samples per class.

E4.justification: V4 adds controlled analyses of unlearning duration versus generation quality (Table 2) and the effect of limited retained-data access (Table 10). These substantially extend investigation of training dynamics and the central data constraint beyond the existing gamma and checkpoint-sensitivity studies, which are retained.

E5.justification: V4 newly identifies Table 1 values as means over three random seeds. V2 provides no corresponding seed-count disclosure, while the numerical values remain identical. This establishes additional reporting, not an explicit increase in runs; neither version supplies dispersion estimates for this table.

E6.justification: Existing main, gamma-sensitivity, CelebA, and checkpoint-table values are retained. V4 substantially expands outcomes through epoch trajectories, five CLIP before/after pairs, baseline runtimes, limited-retained-data results, and Kinkade examples. Table 2 reports Digit-1 PUL increasing from 75.06 to 100.00 while u-FID worsens from 14.43 to 218.83 across epochs. CelebA epoch-cost results disappear from the timing figure.

T1.justification: The Gaussian assumptions, lemmas, theorem, and appendix derivations remain substantively unchanged. The expanded main-text KL decomposition repeats mathematics already present in v2 Appendix A.1.3. V4's lower-bound warning adds interpretation, without supplying a new guarantee or proof.

C1.justification: The first contribution is narrowed from establishing a theoretical connection between machine unlearning and variational inference to proposing a variational framework specifically for diffusion unlearning. The principal claims about data efficiency, computational efficiency, and class/feature unlearning otherwise remain.

C2.justification: New Appendix A.3.1 explicitly acknowledges that minimizing the lower bound need not minimize the original objective. V4 also explains quality deterioration during prolonged optimization through the unbounded plasticity term and identifies missing UnlearnCanvas evaluation as a limitation. Existing mean-field, checkpoint, and feature-entanglement limitations remain.

D1.justification: V4 adds a VDU implementation link in the abstract and Appendix A.4.4, whereas v2 only links underlying models and implementations. It also identifies the CLIP backbone and evaluation epochs. Existing hardware, checkpoint sources, learning rates, and training details are largely unchanged.

R1.justification: V4 adds Zhang et al.'s UnlearnCanvas work and positions its missing evaluation as future work. The related-work discussion otherwise remains substantially unchanged. Consolidating the duplicate Nguyen variational-Bayesian-unlearning references does not remove that prior work.

P1.justification: V4 retitles the paper, separates Preliminaries from the method section, expands diffusion background and the proof sketch, reorders contribution bullets, and adds acknowledgments and subsection headings. Most existing narrative remains recognizably unchanged.

P2.justification: The journal format changes typography, margins, headers, author layout, and algorithm presentation throughout. V4 adds four tables and a Kinkade gallery, reverses metric-column order in the extended results table, and redraws the timing chart without CelebA. A duplicate Van Gogh panel is removed from Figure 8 but remains in Figure 4.

improvement.justification: V4 improves assessability through quantitative feature checks, training-duration and retained-data analyses, baseline timings, and implementation access information. Explicitly acknowledging the lower-bound limitation also improves transparency. These gains remain limited: the theoretical gap is not resolved, three-seed means lack dispersion, and the removed CelebA timing bars leave accompanying four-dataset prose inaccurate. The net effect is a modest quality improvement.
